name: wan-s1-lat
description: Plan 11.3's latency half: a 64-byte request/response probe for ten minutes with a competing bulk flow inside the same tunnel, on the S1 production profile and a real path. This is the run V18 (tx-channel backpressure) is really about — a bulk flow that is allowed to fill the send queue is exactly what makes a small interactive stream wait behind it, and a short path flatters that. iperf3 cannot share a scenario with the pingpong workloads (a kcptun server forwards to one target), so the competing flow is a `bulk` workload. Ports: the tunnel is 29910+ and the pingpong target 22700, not the 29900/22600 defaults, so a WAN run cannot collide with a netns lab that is up on either host — the port check unions the host's listeners with both lab namespaces', and a detached soak owns the defaults inside kr-srv.
